_summary: Stage 2.5 global consolidation, EMT Ch6, 205 notes / 197 highlights. Real cross-block duplicates found: 4 (cards 71, 73, 178, 195). Genuine trivia cuts: 0 (every remaining card carries a fact tested nowhere else). Cross-card give-aways worth fixing: 6, all repaired in place with no card lost. Net after this pass (plus the externally-agreed drop of card 38): 200 notes, all 197 indices still covered.

merges.why: Card 71 (block F, from_idx [69] = the highlighted title of TABLE 6-7 Cardiovascular Values) re-tests exactly what cards 54 and 55 already test from the body text: stroke volume = blood moved in one beat, cardiac output = blood moved in one minute, CO = SV x HR. Card 54 (idx 52,53) and card 55 (idx 54,55) both carry the fact AND the numbers (70-80 mL, 5-6 L) that card 71 omits; card 71's Mechanism line (CO = SV x HR) is already on card 54's and card 55's Back Extra. Card-rules #12: the table is a recap, so card the fact once and keep the clearer phrasing. Card 71's only content not already carded is the table's parenthetical '(left ventricle)' and the note that a weak left ventricle moves less blood per beat -- absorbed into card 54's Back Extra below so nothing goes untested (guards against R4).
merges.revised_Back_Extra:
Distinguish: stroke volume is the per-beat volume, cardiac output the per-minute volume.

Mechanism: the volume comes from one contraction of the left ventricle, so a weak left ventricle moves less blood per beat than a strong one.

merges.why: Cards 62 (block E, idx 61) and 73 (block F, idx 69) define systemic vascular resistance twice, and they literally swap contents: card 62's stem says 'how dilated or constricted the vessels are ... sets the size of the container' with 'excluding the pulmonary vessels' in its Back Extra, while card 73's stem says 'resistance in all vessels excluding the pulmonary vessels' with the container line in its Back Extra. Same claim, two blocks, neither agent could see the other. Card 62 must survive (idx 61 is a singleton -- only card 62 covers it); card 73's idx 69 is the TABLE 6-7 title and stays covered. Card 73's one piece of unique testable content is the pulmonary-vessel exclusion, so the revised card 62 clozes it (c3) rather than demoting it to Back Extra -- otherwise this merge would recreate R4 under-clozing.
merges.revised_Text: {{c1::Systemic vascular resistance (SVR)}} is {{c2::how dilated or constricted the blood vessels are}}, measured across every vessel in the body except {{c3::the pulmonary vessels}}.
merges.revised_Back_Extra:
Mechanism: the higher the systemic vascular resistance, the smaller the container the blood must fill, so the pressure inside the vessels is higher.

Pitfall: SVR describes the vessels' state, not how much blood is in them, so it can change while the blood volume stays exactly the same.

merges.why: Both cards come from the SAME nine-word highlight (idx 190, 'The most common airway obstruction is blockage by the tongue'), both hide the same word, and both use the same hint (::structure). Card 195 wraps it in a scenario ('unconscious, face-up, nothing visible in the mouth, no trauma -- what is blocking the airway?') whose answer is not only card 194's answer but is spelled out in card 194's own Mechanism line ('when a patient loses consciousness the tongue relaxes and sags posteriorly'). That is R6 in its purest form plus R2 fragmentation of a single short highlight, and the Ch6 brief explicitly warns against wrapping a fact in a vignette when the fact does not need one. Card 194 keeps the field-relevant reasoning in its Pitfall (nobody swallows their tongue; a manual airway maneuver alone reopens it).

Card 178 (block M, from_idx [178] = the highlighted title of TABLE 6-12 Endocrine Glands) has three clozes and every one is tested elsewhere: c3 'glucose metabolism / insulin and glucagon' is exactly card 150's c2+c3 (islets of Langerhans produce insulin and glucagon, which regulate blood glucose, from the body text at idx 151); c2 'retroperitoneal space' is card 148's c2 ('behind the peritoneum', idx 148), card 135's c1 ('retroperitoneal', idx 136) and card 180's c2 (idx 179); c1 'pancreas' is the row label. Card-rules #12 -- the table is the recap of facts already carded from the body text. LOWEST-CONFIDENCE ITEM IN THIS VERDICT: the endocrine-table rows (cards 174-179) are a parallel-sibling template, and dropping 178 leaves that set with five glands rather than six. If the caller would rather keep the row intact, the alternative is to keep card 178 unchanged and accept the duplication -- no fact is at risk either way, since idx 178 keeps five sibling cards and every claim survives on cards 150, 135, 148 and 180.

giveaways.why: Card 8 (block A, idx 8, 'A symphysis is a joint at which only slight motion is possible') carries an Ex: line that reproduces card 21 (block B, idx 21) almost word for word: 'the pubic symphysis is the cartilaginous articulation joining the left and right pubic bones, and it limits movement between them.' That single line hands over ALL THREE of card 21's clozes -- c1 pubic symphysis, c2 'cartilaginous joint between the two pubic bones', c3 'slight' motion. Cross-block (A vs B), so neither agent could see it. This is the most complete give-away in the batch: one sibling's Back Extra is the other card's entire answer.
giveaways.fix:
Replace card 8's Back Extra with: "Distinguish: most joints permit a broad range of motion, while a few are fused into solid, immobile bone, such as the cranial bones of the skull.

Ex: the pubic symphysis, which closes the front of the pelvic ring, is named for this limited-motion class of joint." -- keeps the example and the grounding, removes the composition/location that IS card 21's answer.

giveaways.why: Card 84 (block G, idx 79-82) is the classify/fill-the-table card for the adrenergic receptors: beta-1 -> heart -> rate and force increase -> cardiac output rises; beta-2 -> lungs -> bronchi dilate. Card 108 (block H, idx 108,109) prints those answers in its Back Extra: 'Ex: sympathetic stimulation raises heart and respiratory rates, dilates the pupils and the airways...' The same Back Extra's Distinguish line ('a slower, weaker heartbeat') also hands over card 86's c2 pair (parasympathetic makes the heart beat more slowly and more weakly). Cross-block G vs H. Card 84 is the higher-value card of the three, so card 108's Back Extra is the one to trim.
giveaways.fix:
Replace card 108's Back Extra with: "Ex: sympathetic stimulation dilates the pupils, shunts more blood to skeletal muscle, and causes sweating.

Distinguish: parasympathetic effects mirror those, constricting the pupils and promoting digestion." -- all still grounded in the same source list; only the heart-rate/force and airway items (cards 84 and 86's clozes) are removed.

giveaways.why: Card 197 is the scenario card 'soccer player knocked unconscious, no chest or airway injury -- which half of breathing is directly threatened?' with answer {{c1::ventilation}}. Card 201 is the classify card for the three categories, and its Pitfall line says 'weakened respiratory muscles AND A DEPRESSED LEVEL OF CONSCIOUSNESS both land under ventilation.' That sentence is card 197's answer stated as a rule, so card 197 becomes recognition instead of reasoning -- textbook card-rules #13. Both cards are worth keeping (card 197 covers the second clause of idx 191, 'if a patient's level of consciousness is too low, ventilatory problems can occur', which card 196 does not cover), so fix the leak rather than dropping either.
giveaways.fix:
Replace card 201's Back Extra with: "Distinguish: ventilation is moving air in and out, respiration is gas crossing the alveolar membrane, and oxygenation is the quality of the air the patient is breathing.

Pitfall: weakened respiratory muscles land under ventilation too, even though nothing is wrong with the lungs themselves." -- drops only the level-of-consciousness clause.

giveaways.why: Card 168 (block L, idx 172) clozes {{c2::cecum}} for 'the appendix opens into the ___'. That relationship is stated in the VISIBLE stem of card 130 (block J, idx 130: 'the appendix is a small tubular structure attached to the cecum's lower border') and again in card 129's Cue. A visible-stem statement on a sibling is a stronger leak than a Back Extra one, and this is also the same claim carded in two blocks (J and L). The genuinely unique content of card 168 is the length from its own highlight ('It is 3 to 4 inches (8 to 10 cm) long'); the cecum relation was context the L agent imported. Card 168's Distinguish line separately prints card 160's only cloze ('the duodenum ... runs about 12 inches (30 cm)'), so both problems are fixed by the same rewrite. No card is dropped -- idx 172 stays covered by cards 168 and 169.
giveaways.fix:
Card 168 Text -> "The appendix is a tube only {{c1::3 to 4 inches (8 to 10 cm)}} long, attached to the cecum in the right lower quadrant." ; Back Extra -> "Cue: the appendix opens into the cecum, the first part of the large intestine, so its trouble is felt in the right lower quadrant.

Distinguish: the appendix is a blind tube hanging off the cecum, not a segment of the colon itself."

giveaways.why: Card 160 (block L, idx 163) is a single-cloze number card: the duodenum is about {{c1::12 inches (30 cm)}} long. Card 145 (block K, idx 145) prints that exact figure in its Back Extra Distinguish: 'The duodenum is about 12 inches (30 cm), a nearly identical figure for a different tube.' Cross-block K -> L, so neither agent could see it, and because card 160 has only ONE cloze the leak takes away the whole card. (The other half of the same leak, on card 168, is repaired by the card-168 fix above.)
giveaways.fix: Card 145 Back Extra Distinguish -> "Distinguish: the esophagus and the duodenum are nearly the same length, so a figure in inches is easy to attach to the wrong tube." -- keeps the confusable-pair warning that makes the line worth having, without printing card 160's answer.

giveaways.why: Reciprocal cross-block digit leak (K <-> M). Card 153 (idx 156) clozes 'about {{c1::25%}} of the cardiac output' for the liver and its Cue says 'the kidneys take a comparable share, nearly 20% of the heart's output each minute' -- which is card 181's (idx 180) only cloze. Card 181's Distinguish returns the favour: 'the liver takes an even larger share -- roughly 25% of the cardiac output.' Each card hands over the other's answer before it has been earned. This is the only CROSS-BLOCK instance of the chapter-wide reciprocal-Distinguish pattern that I propose touching (see keep_as_is_notes); the comparison itself is worth keeping, only the digits need to go.
giveaways.fix: Card 153 Cue -> "Cue: the kidneys take a comparable but slightly smaller share of the heart's output each minute." ; Card 181 Distinguish -> "Distinguish: the liver takes an even larger share of the cardiac output each minute."

keep_as_is_notes:
HOW MANY REAL DUPLICATES: few. Across 205 cards from 14 blind agents, only FOUR cards are genuine same-fact duplicates (71, 73, 178, 195), and three of those four trace to the same structural cause -- an agent was handed a highlighted TABLE TITLE (idx 69 = Table 6-7 Cardiovascular Values, idx 178 = Table 6-12 Endocrine Glands) and dutifully carded rows that another block had already carded from the body text. That is the recap case card-rules #12 was written for, and it is the one thing to watch for in future fan-outs: whichever agent gets a table-title highlight will re-card its neighbours' facts. Zero cards were cut as trivia -- every remaining card carries at least one fact tested nowhere else, and the ratio only moves from 1.04 to 1.02 notes per highlight.

THE ONE BIG SYSTEMIC PATTERN I DELIBERATELY SPARED -- reciprocal Distinguish lines. Chapter-wide, and independently adopted by every single agent, cards cross-reference their siblings by printing the sibling's clozed answer in a Back Extra Distinguish/Cue/Pitfall line. Examples: card 42 prints card 43's 500 mL; cards 157 and 167 print each other's 90% and 5-10%; cards 188 and 189 print each other's 1-3 min and 4-6 min; the whole block-K fluid-volume web (142/146/149/152/153/156) is explicitly built this way ('Three different fluids, one number'); cards 109/110, 113/114 and 100/101 mirror each other's definitions. I did NOT touch these, for three reasons: (1) parker-preferences.md licenses it directly -- 'Confusable terms get cross-linking Distinguish lines'; (2) every leak sits in Back Extra, which Parker sees only AFTER answering, not in a visible stem; (3) intra-block webs are one agent's coherent design with full sight of its own cards, which is not the blind-fan-out defect I was sent to find. I flagged only the two CROSS-block instances (153<->181, 145->160) where no agent could have known. Worth a ruling from Parker, and possibly a line in card-rules.md: a Distinguish line may name a sibling's concept but should not print a sibling's clozed digits.

CARD 116 -- DO NOT MERGE (near miss). Card 116 ('the exposed surface layer of the epidermis is the {{c1::stratum corneum}}') looks like a thin one-cloze card ripe for merging into card 117, and card 118's Distinguish leaks it ('the stratum corneum (the exposed surface)'). But idx 117 carries a binding user_comment from Parker: 'All I wanna know is that the surface layer is that.' Card 116 is exactly what he asked for. Left untouched, and I did not trim card 118's Distinguish either, since restating what he explicitly wants to know is not a defect here.

SCENARIO CARDS I CHECKED AND SPARED. Card 128 (left flank + lower left rib fractures -> spleen) and card 138 (tenderness at the rib-cage/spine junction -> kidney) are both answerable by chaining two sibling fact-cards, but that chaining IS the reasoning, and the Ch6 brief explicitly licenses scenario cards for 'an organ whose location predicts an injury pattern.' Neither reuses a sibling's Ex: line verbatim, which is what R6 actually forbids. Card 51 (agonal gasps -> ventilations + compressions) tests a treatment no sibling states. Card 197 is kept for the same reason and its leak is repaired above rather than by deletion.

OVER-FRAGMENTATION I JUDGED AND SPARED. Three cards from idx 137 (136 kidney size/position, 137 costovertebral angle definition, 138 the flank scenario) is the densest cluster in the chapter, but the highlight genuinely contains three facts and the CVA definition is prerequisite closure (card-rules #11). Cards 27-31 are six cards from the single muscle table at idx 28 -- a parallel-sibling template, one row each, correctly built. Cards 174-179 are the same for the endocrine table (and this is why merge #4 is my lowest-confidence item). Cards 70/72/74 remain the surviving rows of Table 6-7 after merges #1 and #2, which together with cards 54, 55, 62, 69 cover all eight of its rows.

CROSS-BLOCK OVERLAPS I EXAMINED AND FOUND GENUINELY DISTINCT. Pancreas location is stated on cards 133, 135, 148 and 180, but each tests a different claim (quadrants / retroperitoneal classification + rib-to-L3 span / relation to liver and stomach / the kidneys' position with the pancreas only as a Distinguish) -- no merge. Card 41 (pons adjusts depth of breathing under stress, idx 39) vs card 104's pons row (brainstem's three parts, idx 100/104): different highlights, different claims, kept. Card 39 (hypoxic-drive oxygen sensors) vs card 87 (baroreceptors) share the aortic and carotid sites but test different sensor types; card 87's Distinguish naming the oxygen sensors is exactly the kind of contrast that earns its place. Card 84's Mechanism vs card 174 (adrenals release epinephrine, norepinephrine and cortisol): partial overlap only, cortisol is still real recall. Card 32 (three pharynx sections, respiratory chapter) vs card 143 (oropharynx as the shared food/air tube, digestive chapter): same structure, different claims. Card 151's liver-functions list includes 'makes bile that digests fat', which card 162 also clozes -- but 151 is a cohesive grouped list that must stay whole (parker-preferences 'big lists stay whole') and 162's real content is the liver->gallbladder->duodenum pathway. Cards 55/75/79 all involve 5-6 L or 6 L but test three different quantities (blood circulated per minute, total adult blood volume, cardiac output defended after blood loss).

ONE NOTE FOR THE SEPARATE CARD-180 FIX. While card 180's known R3 leak is being repaired, its Distinguish line ('the pancreas occupies that same space, which is why it is fixed deep in the abdomen and not easily damaged') is a near-verbatim restatement of card 148's stem -- worth rewriting in the same pass.

RESPECTED AS INSTRUCTED, NOT RE-LITIGATED: card 38 dropped in favour of 196 (idx 37 stays on card 37); card 180's R3 leak; the frontal-lobe/prefrontal merge of cards 94 and 98; bile cards 155/162; shock cards 78/204; the RUQ/LUQ quadrant siblings and the hypoxia/hypercapnia pair (cards 192/193 -- note only that card 191's Distinguish defines both of them, which I left alone as part of that intentional template).

COVERAGE AUDIT: after the four drops here plus the externally-agreed drop of card 38, 200 notes remain and all 197 highlight indices are still covered by at least one card. Verified programmatically: idx 69 -> cards 70, 72, 74; idx 178 -> cards 174, 175, 176, 177, 179; idx 190 -> card 194; idx 37 -> card 37. No index falls to zero.
